survey: A cartoon rocket floating against a blue sunburst. There is no ground. The body is a silver cylinder that tapers toward the bottom. It leans to the right and is seen from slightly above in a three-quarter view. A red nose cone sits on top, with a red ring where it meets the body. The ring's front edge dips below its sides, so it is seen from above. The cone's tip leans along the same axis as the body (about the same tilt, roughly 0.29 sideways per unit down). Two round portholes with metal rims sit on the side of the body facing the camera. They are stacked along the body's tilted axis, so the lower one sits further left. Both are almost circles, which fits a cylinder face turned toward the viewer. Two red fins stick out from the lower left and lower right of the body. Each is angled slightly toward the camera, so a bit of its face and thickness shows, which fits a rocket with three fins seen in three-quarter view. At the bottom, a black nozzle band curves the same way as the nose ring, so it is seen from the same viewpoint. A yellow flame comes out of the nozzle along the body axis. Every round band, the body axis, the cone and the fins agree on one camera.
